bears.note: Black locates Ficino's Platonism as the prominent alternative to the Peripatetic conjunction models against which Pico's account of felicity has to be placed.
Ficino's public description of Pico as a fellow Platonist in the 1492 preface, and Black's reading of it as recruitment.

judged.justification: Presents Ficino's 1492 praise as an attempt at enlistment, not a neutral report of agreement.

bears.note: Ficino praises Pico publicly in 1492 as a fellow Platonist and as a pious interpreter of Aristotle.
Distances Pico from Ficino's Platonist-only reading of the intellect controversy.

judged.justification: Qualifies Ficino's presentation of Pico as a Platonist ally.

open.t: How Pico would have argued the intellect conclusions is unknown because the Apologia does not defend them.

bears.note: The commission censured none of the intellect conclusions, so the Apologia is silent on them.

quotes.t: Pico urges his audience to approach the Cherubim ﬁrst, since they will provide the path to the others. They are the “exem- plar” on which human life should be formed.
The example they provide is the method of intellectual ascent, which Pico interprets allegorically from a phrase of Pseudo-Dionysius: “they are cleansed, then illuminated, ﬁnally perfected”.

judged.justification: Ties the top of the human soul to the angelic world, against scholastic psychology.

bears.note: The Commento is Pico's allegorical reading of Benivieni's canzone as an ascent to the first mind.

judged.justification: Places a sabbath as a seventh step beyond intellectual ascent that the soul may not itself take.
Shows the Commento's angelic part carried into the Heptaplus under a new name.
Positions Pico on the identity of the illuminating intellect.

open.t: The direct source of Pico's attribution to Maimonides and Abubacher is unidentified.
Whether Pico used the composite De perfectione naturalis intellectus is uncertain, since no Latin author before Achillini and Nifo is known to cite it.

judged.justification: Shows the Heptaplus as a more cautious restatement of the Commento's claim about direct cognition.
Identifies the seventh exposition's subject with the sabbath of celestial love of the Commento.

bears.note: The Platonists are counted among the several schools of natural felicity that Pico treats as partly valid, not as the single true school.
Pico declines to pick Platonism over the Peripatetic models, which departs from Ficino's Platonist-only settlement.

judged.justification: Supports reading Pico's Heptaplus as neutral between schools on natural felicity.

quotes.t: In so doing, he provides another comment on the structure of the Heptaplus. The ﬁrst six expositions are concerned with natural felicitas, that is, philosophy

The seventh exposition is concerned with supernatural felicitas, that is, religion; as such, it concentrates on the progress of sacred history, from the Fall to the coming of the Messiah and, ﬁnally, redemption.

judged.justification: Reads the sevenfold structure as six natural expositions plus a seventh of a different order, the sabbath.

open.t: Black calls the reference to Averroist unicity in Heptaplus 4.4 veiled and says the most likely interpretation is that it concerns the philosophi iuniores.

judged.justification: Ties the sabbath, the seventh exposition and the ineffable union together as one doctrine.
Places angelic status below the supernatural felicity.
Explains the six-plus-one structure of the Heptaplus by the transcendence of supernatural felicity.

bears.note: Pico's non-partisan handling of the intellect debate contrasts with Ficino's alignment with the Platonist side.

judged.justification: Recasts Pico's felicity doctrine as a mechanism for reconciling disputing schools.
Offers intellectual ascent as the unifying theme of the early works.

bears.note: Mithridates translated Gersonides on the Song of Songs for Pico, who annotated the translation.
The Gersonides commentary in which Pico met the death of the kiss reached him through Mithridates' translation.

judged.justification: Offers Gersonides as a model for the Heptaplus's hermeneutic of ascent.
Frames Genesis as a container of knowledge, not just a guide to acquiring it.
Links the six expositions to natural felicity through the three worlds.
Connects the angelic mode of cognition to the Heptaplus's account of how Moses wrote.
Uses the angelic mind's economy of forms as a model for Mosaic style.
Explains the Heptaplus's exegetical method by Mosaic compression.
Links the last chapter of the Heptaplus to the ascent theme.
Reads the bereshit sentence as a compressed map of the whole work.

bears.note: Mithridates's translation of the Liber combinationum supplies seven of the words Pico derives from bereshit.

open.t: The form in which Pico read Recanati's text is unknown because the manuscript is lost.

bears.note: Mithridates's rendering of ma'amar as verbum may explain how Pico read the sefirotic sentence as a verbal one.

judged.justification: Offers a translation-based mechanism for Pico's setting aside of the sefirot.

open.t: Why Pico left the sefirotic framework of the Conclusiones is unexplained.

black2006-c:068.hedge_words: must remain a matter for speculation

judged.justification: Makes a specific kabbalistic text, not display, the source of the bereshit method.

quotes.t: There is one exposition for each of the worlds; one exposition for man, who is “a fourth world, in which are also found all the things that are in the other worlds”
and a ﬁnal exposition corresponding to the sabbath.
since the expositions are distributed into seven books, and each book is divided into seven chapters, everything corresponds to the seven days of creation.
so each of our expositions in its seventh chapter always turns aside towards Christ, who is both the end of the law and our sabbath, our rest, our felicitas.

judged.justification: Reverses the received order: the sabbath, not the content, is said to have dictated the sevenfold form.

black2006-c:076.hedge_words: appears to be the formative element

judged.justification: Says form governs content in the Heptaplus's structure.
Gives the structural key: same text, seven frameworks.
Explains why a sevenfold work comments on six days: the sabbath is a form, not a text.
Reads sabbath as the Heptaplus's form.
Identifies the sabbath with supernatural felicity and with the redirection of the narrative to the future.

bears.note: Black locates the Heptaplus's sabbath ideas in Jewish esoteric material that Mithridates made available to Pico.

judged.justification: Roots the sabbath form in Mithridates's Kabbalistic corpus rather than in Christian tradition alone.
Connects sabbath, jubilee and supernatural felicity.

open.t: Whether Nahmanides's introduction influenced Pico is undecided; Black calls it a matter of speculation.

judged.justification: Ties Pico's claim that Moses portrayed an image of the world to the tradition of the forty-nine gates.
Offers a specific source for the seven-by-seven form: the forty-nine gates of understanding.
Gives Proclus and Pseudo-Dionysius, not fourfold exegesis, as the source of the Heptaplus's hermeneutics.
Identifies the angelic mode of cognition as the goal of the Heptaplus's ascent.
Puts angels at the top of Moses's ascent and Pico's decoding project.

quotes.t: Pico’s project was to ﬁnd and interpret the ways in which this knowledge was encoded in Moses’s text.
whereas average human understanding requires a large number of forms with which to understand concepts ‘discursively’

text shows how the same concepts can be expressed with very few ‘forms’, that is, words. As such, it represents the ‘simplicity’ of forms by which angels (and, by extension, prophets) can understand things normally out of human reach.

judged.justification: Ties Mosaic economy of language to the angelic mode of understanding.
Gives Black's answer to how the Heptaplus should be read: as Dionysian anagogy.
States the work's subject as cosmology, not cosmogony.
Places the Heptaplus outside the Christian exegetical mainstream of its time.
Denies that the Heptaplus fits the Pico-as-Renaissance-symbol reading.
Gives Black's consolidated model of the soul's ascent from the Commento to the Heptaplus.

bears.note: The Gersonides commentary was among the texts Mithridates translated for Pico.

judged.justification: Gives the sabbath as the reason and the kabbalistic texts as the source of the sevenfold form.
Offers the forty-nine gates as the model for the seven-by-seven structure.

open.t: Whether the Heptaplus's discretion reflects the trial or a syncretist aim is left open by Black.

bears.note: Black suggests the 1487 affair and the condemnation may explain the Heptaplus's discretion about scholastic psychology.

judged.justification: Links the tone of the Heptaplus to the aftermath of the trial, as one hypothesis.

bears.note: Pico's strategy of not arbitrating between schools contrasts with Ficino's Platonist alignment described earlier in Black's argument.

judged.justification: States Pico's handling of school disputes as defusion by the two-fold felicity.
